THE BRAIN BEHIND THE BUZZ

Run the real experiment.

This 3D garden is a stylized demo. The separate Python lab runs a real 129-neuron MaleCNS circuit connected to a tethered FlyBody in MuJoCo. It is a foreleg experiment, not autonomous walking or lifting.

  1. Install Python 3.12 and Git on your computer.
  2. Download the simulation branch and install its dependencies:
git clone --branch connectome-body-lab https://github.com/vibejedi/flygains.git
cd flygains
python -m venv .venv
# macOS / Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
# Windows PowerShell:
# .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r simulation/requirements.txt
git clone https://github.com/TuragaLab/flybody.git data/flybody
git -C data/flybody checkout d015e9bfe441bd90ae431bac24c55cb74bdbce26
python -m simulation.server --circuit samples/mcns-dna02 --flybody data/flybody

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8765 on that computer. The real physics lab is already 3D. The green garden shown here uses a different stylized fly model.

To run continuously on this public website, the Python process needs a persistent host plus an authenticated HTTPS connection to the frontend. That connection is not deployed yet; Vercel currently serves only this garden.

Your own equipment

Create GLB/glTF visuals in Blender. Keep bars, plates, and moving parts separate. Physics needs simple collision shapes, masses and joints too. Custom equipment import is not included yet.

Equipment asset guide ↗

Demo gains are fictional. It runs only while this page is active and resets on reload. The garden's motion does not come from the MaleCNS spiking experiment.
